theories.title: famfs_kill_sb holds dax device reference that pins dentries open
theories.description: famfs_kill_sb calls fs_put_dax() or similar DAX teardown AFTER kill_char_super()/generic_shutdown_super(). If the dax device reference or holder is released after shrink_dcache_for_umount runs, something in the DAX/holder path may hold dentry references that prevent cleanup.
evidence_for: famfs_kill_sb is in the call trace just after kill_char_super
famfs uses a dax device (fsdev_dax module loaded)
Multiple dentries are affected, suggesting a systematic reference leak not a one-off
suggested_next_steps: Read famfs_kill_sb: does it release the dax device before or after kill_char_super?
Check if fs_dax_get/fs_put_dax or dax holder ops hold dentry references

theories.title: famfs inode or file objects hold dentry references past unmount
theories.description: famfs may store dentry or file references in per-inode private data (famfs_file_meta or famfs_fs_info). If these are not released before generic_shutdown_super() calls shrink_dcache_for_umount(), dentries will still have nonzero refcounts.
evidence_for: Dentry refcount is exactly 1 — consistent with one unreleased reference in famfs private data
Multiple files affected — suggests a per-file reference stored systematically
famfs_evict_inode frees i_private; if called too late, dentry refs may linger
suggested_next_steps: Read famfs_evict_inode: does it drop any dentry references?
Read famfs_file_meta / famfs_fs_info: do they store dentry or file pointers?
Check famfs_fill_super for any stored dentries or file references

theories.title: famfs superblock metadata inode/dentry not released before shrink_dcache
theories.description: famfs may create special inodes at mount time (e.g., a .log or metadata inode) and store a dentry for them in famfs_fs_info. If kill_sb doesn't drop these before generic_shutdown_super, shrink_dcache_for_umount finds them still referenced.
evidence_for: famfs has a log/superblock file concept in the standalone design
The dentry name 'pcq_lib.c' looks like a regular famfs file, but the pattern of multiple dentries affected is consistent with all files having a pinned reference
suggested_next_steps: Read famfs_fs_info structure for any dentry/file/inode pointer fields
Read famfs_kill_sb for dentry drops before kill_char_super
